Package io.thymekit

Class Element<K>

java.lang.Object
io.thymekit.Element<K>
All Implemented Interfaces:
Composable<K>
public final class Element<K> extends Object implements Composable<K>
The single currency of composition: every element's build() returns one. Elements go onto a canvas (PageModel), into containers and into larger elements.

K is a phantom marker — the factory class that produced the element (Element<Heading>). There is no type hierarchy: a new element is just a factory, and the type it produces exists for free. Wide points accept Element<?>; narrow points name the marker, so the compiler rejects a combination only where it is genuinely meaningless.

Inside is a descriptor: the address of the element's adapter fragment (template :: fragment(e)) plus data. Templates read asMap(), so the adapter contract does not depend on typing: the data is untyped, the marker is typed.

    • assertOutline

      public static void assertOutline(Collection<?> roots)
      Outline guard, run by the canvas before a page is rendered. Two things are checked, and both are defects a reader or a crawler would meet on the finished page rather than opinions about style:
      • at most one first-level heading — the title of a page is one thing, not several;
      • no level skipped — a page that uses h4 while nothing on it is an h3 has a hole in its outline, and a screen reader walking headings falls straight through it;
      • no level outside h1..h6 — html has six, and the adapter renders nothing at all for a seventh, which is the kind of silence a page should never ship with.

      A level is read however it was written into the descriptor — as a number or as text. The factories always write a number, but an element minted by hand may not, and a guard that only understood one of the two would have let a second H1 through while the adapter happily rendered it.

      The levels a page uses have to be contiguous; where in the flow they stand is not the guard's business, so nesting an element deeper never trips it. Illustration subtrees are skipped — a sample framed for display is not page structure — and a page with no headings at all is legal.

      The guarantee stops where the kit stops. A heading an author wrote inside markdown is not seen here — that text is data and arrives as HTML long after this runs. Such headings are lowered under the page by MarkdownRenderer instead, so content does not declare a second H1; a gap the author left inside the text travels with it, and neither this guard nor the renderer closes it.

    • settle

      public static <K> Element<K> settle(Composable<K> composable, String name)
      Whatever becomes an element, settled at once and never before: a place that takes a Composable builds it here, keeps the element and forgets the maker. That is the rule the kit follows everywhere — accept what becomes an element, store only what has become one.
